h1: Baan Ingkhao Resort — a garden hillside resort with a pool that's still very easy on the wallet
intro: If you want a Muak Lek stay with a garden feel, plenty of trees and a pool for the kids — without paying a lot — Baan Ingkhao Resort is a small Khao Yai-foothills resort that keeps prices low. Rooms are wooden-floor villas scattered through the gardens, there's a swimming pool, a children's playground and a BBQ area, and the morning air is cool and fresh. Honestly, this is a simple garden resort rather than a polished one — but for a weekend family trip where you want a pool, leafy grounds and an affordable rate, it fits nicely. From approx. THB 1,200/night.

body.html: The thing guests mention most about Baan Ingkhao Resort is the garden, hillside feel. The resort sits in leafy grounds with plenty of trees, and the rooms are wooden-floor villas tucked into the shade. Mornings are cool and quiet, and several reviews say waking up to the garden air feels genuinely relaxing — nothing like staying in a town-centre block. It suits travellers who want to slip away somewhere peaceful, but still close to Bangkok.

What wins families over at this little resort is the swimming pool. Real reviews describe the water as clear and clean, a good size for children, with a small slide that the kids enjoy. Beyond the pool there's a playground, a BBQ area, karaoke, an on-site restaurant and free bicycles for riding around the grounds — a fair amount to keep a family occupied, at a price that stays gentle.
"A lovely small resort with a pool the kids loved, clean rooms, a good breakfast, clear pool water, helpful staff and easy parking."

The location works well for exploring Muak Lek. The resort sits along Highway 2089 in the Muak Lek district, about 8 km from Muak Lek Waterfall, and right in the Khao Yai foothills, so you can drive on to dairy farms, vineyards and cafés in the area with ease. It's roughly a two-hour drive up from Bangkok — an easy base for a hill-country road trip with an overnight stay.

The honest part is that this is a small, homestay-style garden resort. It started life as Ing Khao Homestay, and some reviews note that the family rooms feel a touch pricey for what you get, that a few of the playground pieces look dated, and that things can be quiet on-site in low season. Staff service draws mixed feedback — some guests found them helpful, others felt the welcome was a little flat. If you're expecting a large, full-service branded resort, this isn't it; but if you can take the small-resort scale in exchange for a budget rate, it still does the job.

On price, standard villa rooms on the booking platforms start around THB 1,200–3,500/night depending on season and room size, with the family rooms sitting at the upper end. The overall score from real reviews lands in the good range, around 7.8 (some platforms rate it higher among recent guests). Location, garden atmosphere, room cleanliness and breakfast score well, while the weaker points are family-room value and the limited facilities you'd expect from a small resort.

Bottom line, drawn from real guest sentiment: Baan Ingkhao Resort suits families and couples who want a quiet garden resort, a pool and an affordable rate more than travellers after a large resort or modern designer rooms. Set your expectations to match what it is — a small garden hillside resort at a low price — and a Muak Lek weekend here passes by just fine.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Baan Ingkhao Resort, Muak Lek, Saraburi

faq.q: Where is Baan Ingkhao Resort and what's nearby?
faq.a: The resort sits at 91 Moo 8, Highway 2089, Tambon Muak Lek, Muak Lek District, Saraburi, in the Khao Yai foothills. It's about 8 km from Muak Lek Waterfall and around 29 km from Pak Chong. It's roughly a two-hour drive from Bangkok.

faq.q: How much does Baan Ingkhao Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Villa rooms start from approx. THB 1,200/night, ranging through the Thai Villa, Deluxe Villa and a villa for three up to a family room around THB 3,500. Prices vary by season and room size — always compare a few platforms before you book.

faq.q: Does Baan Ingkhao Resort have a pool, and is it good for kids?
faq.a: Yes — there's a garden swimming pool with clear, clean water and a small slide. Real reviews say the kids love it. There's also a playground and free bicycles, which is one of the main reasons families choose to stay here.

faq.q: Who is Baan Ingkhao Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a strong fit for families and couples who want a quiet garden resort, a pool and a budget rate. The leafy hillside grounds and cool morning air make it restful. It suits a relaxed Muak Lek road trip on a budget more than travellers after a large resort or modern, designer rooms.

faq.q: What condition are the rooms and service in at Baan Ingkhao Resort?
faq.a: Honestly, from real reviews: most rooms are clean with a pleasant garden atmosphere, but this is a small homestay-style resort — a few playground pieces look dated, and the family rooms can feel pricey. Staff service draws mixed feedback, so we'd suggest confirming the room details before booking.

faq.q: What's the easiest way to get to Baan Ingkhao Resort?
faq.a: Driving yourself is easiest, as the resort sits along Highway 2089 outside town. From Bangkok, take the Mittraphap highway toward Muak Lek, about a two-hour drive. Having a car also makes touring Muak Lek Waterfall, the dairy farm and area cafés far smoother.
